description: Science of Reading aligned level specifications - comprehensive phonics through fluent reading

principles.oneChangeRule: Each level introduces only ONE new element
principles.sightWordDiscipline: Explicitly listed, cumulative caps by band
principles.typographyControl: Single-storey a/g until C-levels, large x-height early
principles.orthographicMapping: Target words appear 4+ times for automatic recognition

A.name: Pre-Reader / Emergent
A.purpose: Visual discrimination, print awareness, letter mastery

A0.name: Concept of Print
A0.readerCan: Handle books, track left-to-right, recognize print carries meaning
A0.storyGuidance: Wordless or 1-2 word labels. Pattern books. Pictures carry all meaning.

A1.name: Letter Recognition
A1.readerCan: Recognize and name target letters, distinguish shapes
A1.storyGuidance: Labels only: 'A [noun]' or 'I [verb]'. One word per page.

A2.name: CV/VC Words + Patterns

constraints.case: Sentence-initial caps, lowercase for known letters

A2.wordRepetition: Pattern word changes, frame stays same
A2.storyGuidance: Repetitive frame: 'I see the ___.' or 'The ___ sat.' Only one word changes.

A3.name: Mixed Case Sentences
A3.readerCan: Read lowercase letters, track 3-4 word sentences

constraints.illustrationRule: Supports but doesn't give away text

A3.storyGuidance: Simple declaratives with slight variation. 'The cat is here. The cat is on it.'

A4.name: Emergent Bridge
A4.storyGuidance: Bridge to phonics. Simple narrative: character + action + outcome.

B1.name: CVC Short a, i
B1.readerCan: Decode CVC words with short a and i vowels

phonicsPatterns: CVC short a: cat, hat, sat, man, can, bat, rat, map, nap
CVC short i: sit, hit, big, pig, fin, pin, dip, bit, fit

B1.phonemicAwareness: Segment and blend CVC with short a/i
B1.storyGuidance: Simple action narrative. 'The cat sat. The cat ran. I see the cat!'

B2.name: CVC Short o, u, e
B2.readerCan: Decode CVC words with all five short vowels

phonicsPatterns: CVC short o: hot, pot, dog, fog, mop, top, got, not
CVC short u: cup, pup, mud, bug, hug, run, sun, fun
CVC short e: bed, red, pet, hen, get, let, ten, pen

B2.storyGuidance: Character wants something, gets it. Emotional range: fun, sad, mad.

B3.name: Final Blends + FLOSS
B3.readerCan: Decode words with final consonant blends and doubled consonants

phonicsPatterns: -nd: and, hand, sand, bend, pond
-mp: jump, bump, camp, lamp, stomp
-st: best, fast, must, list, just
-nt: ant, went, hunt, bent
-nk: pink, bank, sunk, think
-ft: left, soft, gift
-lp: help, yelp

B3.storyGuidance: Action stories: jump, stomp, bump. Suspense: 'What was that?'

B4.name: Initial Blends
B4.readerCan: Decode words beginning with consonant blends

phonicsPatterns: l-blends: black, clap, flag, glad, plan, slip, blue, club
r-blends: brick, crab, drip, frog, grin, trap, tree, from
s-blends: stop, step, swim, snap, spell, skip, smell, sled

B4.storyGuidance: Characters can swim, skip, trip, grab. Two characters interact.

B5.name: Digraphs
B5.readerCan: Decode consonant digraphs (two letters = one sound)

phonicsPatterns: sh: ship, shop, fish, wish, shell, shut, trash
ch: chip, chat, much, rich, such, chin, chest
th: this, that, then, with, them, thin, thick
wh: when, what, which, where, why, white
ck: back, kick, rock, duck, stick, black, truck
ng: ring, sing, song, long, hung, king, thing

B5.storyGuidance: Dialogue natural now. 'She said, "What is that?"' Questions in narrative.

B6.name: Silent E (CVCe)
B6.readerCan: Decode long vowel words with magic e pattern

phonicsPatterns: a_e: cake, make, lake, safe, game, name, came, take
i_e: bike, like, time, hide, ride, five, nine, side
o_e: home, bone, note, hope, stone, those, woke, rose
u_e: cube, cute, huge, tube, mule, June, rule, use

B6.phonemicAwareness: Distinguish CVC from CVCe (short vs long)
B6.storyGuidance: Names with silent e (Jake, Kate, Mike). 'Kate made a cake at home.'

B7.name: Vowel Teams
B7.readerCan: Decode common vowel team patterns for long vowels

phonicsPatterns: ai: rain, wait, tail, train, paint, mail
ay: day, play, say, stay, way, may, gray
ee: see, tree, feet, sleep, green, keep, need
ea: read, eat, sea, team, beach, clean, dream
oa: boat, coat, road, goat, foam, load, toast
ow (long): snow, grow, show, slow, flow, know, low

B7.phonemicAwareness: Identify vowel team as single vowel sound
B7.storyGuidance: Weather, seasons work well. 'The rain came. We had to stay. Then the sun came out to play.'

B8.name: Diphthongs + Complex Vowels
B8.readerCan: Decode diphthongs and remaining vowel patterns

phonicsPatterns: oi: oil, coin, boil, join, point, noise, voice
oy: boy, toy, joy, enjoy, annoy
ou: out, loud, cloud, sound, found, house, mouse
ow (as in cow): cow, how, now, down, town, brown, owl
oo (long): moon, soon, food, pool, school, room, cool
oo (short): book, look, good, wood, foot, cook, took
aw/au: saw, draw, paw, claw, cause, because, taught

B8.phonemicAwareness: Identify diphthong glide (two sounds in one)
B8.storyGuidance: Animals (owl, cow, mouse), outdoor settings. 'The boy found a coin by the brook.'

B9.name: R-Controlled Vowels

phonicsPatterns: ar: car, barn, farm, star, dark, park, yard, hard, start
or: for, corn, horse, storm, short, sport, fort, north
er: her, fern, after, never, over, under, water
ir: bird, first, girl, shirt, dirt, third, stir
ur: turn, burn, hurt, nurse, purple, turtle, Thursday
sightWords: Previous + where, were, here, there, their

B9.phonemicAwareness: Recognize r-controlled as distinct vowel sounds
B9.storyGuidance: Farm, nature, adventure. Multiple scenes. 'After the storm, the girl went to the barn to find her horse.'

C1.name: Silent Letters
C1.readerCan: Decode words with silent letter patterns

phonicsPatterns: kn-: knee, knife, knight, know, knock, knit, knot
wr-: wrap, write, wrong, wrist, wreck, wring
gn-: gnaw, gnat, gnome, sign, design
-mb: climb, lamb, thumb, comb, dumb, numb, bomb
gh: night, right, light, might, fight, bright, thought, through

C1.storyGuidance: Knights, castles, mysteries. 'The knight knew he had to write a sign.'

C2.name: Soft C and G
C2.readerCan: Decode soft c (before e, i, y) and soft g patterns

phonicsPatterns: Soft c (ce, ci, cy): face, race, place, ice, nice, city, pencil, circus, cycle
Soft g (ge, gi, gy): age, cage, page, stage, giant, magic, gym, energy
-dge: edge, bridge, fudge, badge, judge, ledge, ridge, hedge
constraints.rule: c and g are soft before e, i, y; hard before a, o, u

C2.storyGuidance: Cities, stages, magic. 'The giant stood on the bridge near the village.'

C3.name: Two-Syllable Closed
C3.readerCan: Divide and decode VC/CV pattern words

phonicsPatterns: VC/CV division: rab-bit, kit-ten, hap-pen, but-ton, mit-ten, sud-den
Double consonant: better, butter, dinner, funny, happy, puppy, silly, ladder
constraints.syllableRule: When two consonants between vowels, divide between them

C3.storyGuidance: Chapter-style. 'The kitten was hidden in the basket. It happened so suddenly!'

C4.name: Two-Syllable Open + Consonant-le
C4.readerCan: Decode V/CV pattern and consonant-le syllables

phonicsPatterns: V/CV open: pa-per, ti-ger, ro-bot, pi-lot, o-pen, e-ven, mo-ment, si-lent
Consonant-le: ap-ple, lit-tle, pur-ple, tur-tle, sim-ple, mid-dle, puz-zle, bot-tle
Compound words: sunshine, bedroom, homework, outside, birthday, airplane
constraints.syllableRule: When one consonant between vowels, first try dividing before it (open syllable)

C4.storyGuidance: Robots, pilots, adventures. 'The purple turtle hid under the table.'

C5.name: Contractions + Compounds
C5.readerCan: Read contractions and compound words fluently

phonicsPatterns: Contractions with not: can't, won't, don't, didn't, isn't, wasn't, couldn't, wouldn't, shouldn't
Contractions with will: I'll, you'll, he'll, she'll, we'll, they'll
Contractions with is/has: it's, he's, she's, that's, what's
Contractions with am/are: I'm, you're, we're, they're
Compound recognition: into, upon, without, however, anyone, everyone, something, everything

C5.storyGuidance: Natural dialogue. 'I can't find it anywhere! Where'd it go?'

C6.name: Inflectional Endings

phonicsPatterns: -s/-es: cats, dogs, boxes, wishes, matches
-ed (3 sounds): jumped (/t/), played (/d/), wanted (/ed/)
-ing: running, jumping, hoping, making (drop e), sitting (double)
-er comparative: bigger, faster, smaller, taller
-est superlative: biggest, fastest, smallest, tallest
spellingRules: -ed sounds: /t/ after voiceless, /d/ after voiced, /ed/ after t or d

C6.storyGuidance: Past tense narratives. 'She wanted the biggest cookie. She jumped and grabbed it!'

C7.name: Derivational Suffixes
C7.readerCan: Decode common derivational suffixes that change word meaning/part of speech

phonicsPatterns: -ful (full of): careful, helpful, beautiful, wonderful, hopeful, peaceful
-less (without): careless, helpless, hopeless, fearless, endless
-ness (state of): kindness, darkness, happiness, sadness, illness
-ment (action/result): movement, payment, treatment, amazement
-ly (manner): quickly, slowly, carefully, quietly, suddenly, finally
-tion/-sion: action, nation, station, mission, vision, decision
constraints.morphologyFocus: Identify base word + suffix, understand meaning change

C7.storyGuidance: Character emotions and motivations. 'She felt hopeless at first, but suddenly found the solution.'

C8.name: Prefixes
C8.readerCan: Decode common prefixes and understand how they modify meaning

phonicsPatterns: un- (not, opposite): unhappy, unfair, unkind, unlock, untie, unsafe
re- (again): return, reread, rewrite, rebuild, replay, redo
pre- (before): preview, prepay, preheat, preschool
dis- (not, opposite): disagree, disappear, dislike, discover, disable
mis- (wrongly): mistake, misread, misspell, misunderstand
in-/im-/il-/ir- (not): incorrect, impossible, illegal, irregular

C8.storyGuidance: Problem-solving, overcoming. 'She had to redo the impossible task. But she didn't give up.'

D1.name: Sentence Variety + Dialogue
D1.readerCan: Read complex sentences and extended dialogue fluently

syntaxPatterns: Complex: 'Although it was late, they kept going.'
Dialogue with varied tags: asked, replied, whispered, shouted
constraints.punctuation: Commas in complex sentences, dialogue punctuation mastery

D1.storyGuidance: Character-driven with rich dialogue. Multiple speakers distinguished by voice.

D2.name: Inference + Chapter Books

constraints.structure: Chapter books with 4-6 page chapters, cliffhangers

D2.storyGuidance: Show don't tell. 'Her hands trembled as she reached for the handle.' (inference: nervous)

D3.name: Latin Roots
D3.readerCan: Use Latin root knowledge to decode and understand unfamiliar words

rootPatterns: struct (build): structure, construct, instruct, destruction, infrastructure
port (carry): transport, import, export, support, report, portable
dict (say): predict, dictionary, dictate, contradict, verdict
ject (throw): project, reject, inject, eject, subject, object
rupt (break): erupt, interrupt,rupt, disrupt, bankrupt, corrupt
tract (pull): attract, subtract, tractor, extract, contract
spec (see): inspect, respect, spectacle, spectacular, prospect

D3.storyGuidance: Historical, construction, discovery themes. 'The architect inspected the ancient structure.'

D4.name: Greek Roots
D4.readerCan: Use Greek root knowledge for scientific and academic vocabulary

rootPatterns: graph (write): paragraph, biography, photograph, autograph, geography
phon (sound): telephone, symphony, microphone, phonics, cacophony

D4.storyGuidance: Science fiction, exploration, biography. 'The biologist used her microscope to study the organism.'

D5.name: Figurative Language

literaryDevices: Simile: 'brave as a lion', 'quick as lightning'
Metaphor: 'time is money', 'life is a journey'
Hyperbole: 'I've told you a million times'
Idioms: 'break the ice', 'piece of cake', 'under the weather'

D5.storyGuidance: Literary fiction. 'The old house groaned in protest as the storm raged outside.'

D6.name: Grade-Level Prose
D6.readerCan: Read grade-level texts independently with full comprehension
D6.storyGuidance: Full literary complexity. Open endings possible. Themes reward reflection. 'Coming of age' narratives.

oneChangeRule.description: Each level introduces only ONE major element

sightWordProgression.bandD: No new explicit teaching - absorbed through reading

typography.bandsAB: Single-storey 'a' and 'g', large x-height, no decorative fonts

wordRepetition.bandsAB: Target pattern words appear 4+ times (orthographic mapping)

illustrationGuidelines.bandA: Illustrations carry primary meaning, directly match text
illustrationGuidelines.bandB: Illustrations support but don't give away decodable words

assessmentCheckpoints.bandTransitions: Mastery assessment before advancing to next band
